next_review: In 12 months, and after the scribe pilot ends
why: We want AI to lift routine charting and writing off your plate. We must protect patient privacy and keep people in charge of care.
who_it_covers: Everyone who works or volunteers here, including contractors and board members.

tools.name: AI scribe from our health record vendor
tools.approved_for: Three-provider pilot with a signed business associate agreement; visit notes only, and it may hold patient information.

new_tools: Ask first before adding any tool, plugin, agent or AI feature, even inside software we own. Approvers check privacy first.
accounts: Use your work account. Turn off any setting that lets the vendor train on what you type.
allowed_uses: Pilot providers: let the approved scribe listen to visits and draft the note.
Pilot providers: edit the scribe's draft so it matches the visit.
Pilot providers: start from the scribe's draft instead of a blank note, to finish charting sooner.

needs_approval.use: Tool that could touch patient information (business associate agreement first)
Any other new tool or use

protected_information: Passwords and logins never go in. Nothing else goes in unless the tool is approved above. Covered by HIPAA: diagnoses, medications, behavioral health notes, HIV status, reproductive health, immigration status, insurance numbers. Also substance use treatment records (extra federal protection), income documents, staff files, donor lists.
off_limits: No patient information in any tool without a signed business associate agreement. No exceptions.
Never let AI make a clinical decision. A clinician decides and signs.
check_before_it_goes_out: Providers read every word of a scribe note before signing.
Whoever sends AI-assisted work owns it. Check facts, names, numbers and tone; clinicians review patient handouts.
decisions_about_people: AI may only draft or help someone look things up. People decide who gets care.
A person decides sliding fee eligibility from the documents.
being_open: Tell patients when the scribe is listening. They can say no; use the verbal consent script.
If we ever add a website chatbot, it must say it is not a person.
if_something_goes_wrong: Tell Nadia right away if patient information may have gone into an AI tool.
Nadia decides if it is a breach and runs the HIPAA process. Reporting a mistake is expected, never punished.
who_owns_this: The compliance committee reviews this policy; the board approves it and changes. Staff get it at hire and yearly.
open_questions: After the pilot, do we roll the scribe out to all providers, and should behavioral health use it at all?
May staff use ChatGPT, OpenEvidence, UpToDate AI search or Google Translate, with no patient information, and for which tasks?
May AI suggest billing codes or help with Spanish patient materials, and who approves and checks that?
What do we tell HRSA and state funders about AI use, and who owns this policy day to day?
